Name: Sunwapta Falls
Description: First stop heading south from Jasper. Powerful canyon waterfall with turquoise water. Easy 20 min roadside stop. Don't skip it — sets the tone for the Parkway.

Name: Wilcox Pass
Description: Best hike on the entire Icefields Parkway. Wide open alpine pass with close unobstructed views of the Athabasca Glacier and the full Columbia Icefield. 8 km return, 335m gain — allow 3 hrs. Trailhead is directly across from the Columbia Icefield Centre. Do not skip this.

Name: Columbia Icefield / Athabasca Glacier toe
Description: Walk down the marked path to the toe of the Athabasca Glacier and touch ancient ice. Interpretive posts show how far the glacier extended in past decades — a stark visual record of climate change. Stay on marked paths only; do not venture onto the glacier.

Name: Parker Ridge
Description: Fastest high-value hike on the Icefields Pkwy — panoramic view of the Saskatchewan Glacier from an exposed ridge. 4.8 km return, 250m gain. Good backup if Wilcox Pass is weather-affected, or add it if energy allows.

Name: Peyto Lake viewpoint
Description: Wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake viewed from high above — one of the most photographed spots in Canada. Short paved walk 800m, 70m gain from parking lot. Do not rush past this.

Name: Bow Lake
Description: Pull off and walk to the lakeshore. Flat turquoise lake beneath Crowfoot Glacier — excellent in afternoon light on the southbound drive. 15 min stop.
